shaders.name: Tonal mesh
shaders.blurb: Four-stop mesh of primary, secondary, tertiary, and surface. The seed is the lighting.
shaders.use: Hero surfaces, theme lab, empty states

shaders.name: Paper grain
shaders.blurb: Film grain on a tonal wash. Reads as paper, not noise-for-noise.

shaders.name: Elevation light
shaders.blurb: M3 elevation as a lighting model: key from the top-left, tinted ambient, contact shade.

shaders.name: Aurora
shaders.blurb: Slow seed-hue bands. Use on a hero, never as a full-page wallpaper.

shaders.name: Spotlight
shaders.blurb: Pointer-driven key light. Follows the cursor; falls back to a rest pose.
shaders.use: Interactive cards, icon grids, hover chrome

shaders.name: Iridescent rim
shaders.blurb: Spectral edge lighting that shifts with the seed. Think oil on water, not rainbow chrome.
shaders.use: Selected chips, premium cards, icon tiles

shaders.name: Halftone
shaders.blurb: Print shading. Dot size follows a tonal ramp of the seed.
shaders.use: Editorial posters, empty illustrations, print mocks

shaders.name: Caustics
shaders.blurb: Light through water, tinted with primary. Slow and shallow, not a lava lamp.

shaders.name: Ripple field
shaders.blurb: M3 state-layer ripple as a field. Click or rest on a breathing ring.
shaders.use: Buttons, list items, touch feedback studies

shaders.name: Ordered dither
shaders.blurb: Bayer 4×4 shading into two tonal roles. Print-room, not 8-bit nostalgia.
shaders.use: Low-ink posters, data ink, reduced palettes
